purpose: Make retry behavior provable by declaring idempotency, replay, late-duplicate, precondition and operation-status semantics per operation family. The audited core runs two distinct ledgers — the generic HTTP ledger replays for 24 hours while business-record commands use an application ledger with a 7-day default replay window — yet one shared header description promises 24 hours for every mutation. Adoption makes the per-family declaration the normative contract and demotes shared header prose to non-normative text; no window value below is invented, each is observed in the audited source.

families.title: General HTTP mutations
families.summary: Content, content types, workflows, navigation, identity, settings, extensions, automation and plan mutations that pass the generic persistent HTTP idempotency ledger keyed by subject, operation and key.

families.title: Generated business record commands
families.summary: Create, update, delete, archive, restore, relation and document commands on generated business records; these routes bypass the generic HTTP ledger and use the application ledger with installation-configurable windows.

families.title: Custom business actions
families.summary: Typed custom actions published by extensions on business records; the executor keeps its own one-day replay path with the exact contract-validated input bound to the operation key.

families.title: Business search and custom views
families.summary: The bounded read-only query document and typed custom views; read-only by contract, so no idempotency key is consumed and requests are freely retryable.

contradictions: The shared OpenAPI Idempotency-Key parameter and docs/rest-api.md promise a 24-hour replay for every mutation, while the business-record application ledger defaults to 7-day replay with 30-day retention and custom actions keep a one-day path; adoption must scope each statement to its family.

The general HTTP ledger silently executes a late duplicate as a new request after its window, while the business ledger refuses it as window-elapsed; a client cannot handle both correctly without a per-family declaration.

User updates carry an optimistic version in the JSON document while content, navigation and business records use strong If-Match validators; the shared description does not say which form an operation needs.
security_invariants: A replayed response is byte-stable except for declared replay markers and never re-contains a secret-once value.
Key reuse with different request bytes, authority, scope or definition is refused, never executed.
A replay is refused when the replaying credential differs from the credential that started the operation.
The client retains one key per user intent until a terminal outcome is known and never mints a new key because a request timed out.
Replay windows are declared by the server; a client never assumes a longer window than the family declares.
Idempotency records disclose no request or response content to later callers beyond the replayed response itself.
